newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher despite Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher despite Deng's death.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Thursday as investors showed strong confidence in the market's prospects while shrugging off the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
The weighted index rebounded from an earlier fall to close 21.19 points or 0.28 percent higher at 7,678.04.
Turnover was a frantic T$153.19 billion.
The market rebounded from late morning trade after the government pledged to implement market stabilisation measures.
Government spokesman Su Chi said after a cabinet meeting that the government would launch measures and had prepared funds to support the market against a potential plunge.
The stock market, buoyed by widespread hopes of an economic recovery, has finished higher in 12 of the past 14 sessions and gained more than 500 points over that span.
Brokers said investors had already reacted to rumours of Deng's failing health which hit the market several days ago.

"Some investors had been worried that the government would step in to stop the market's recent sharp growth, but there is no way it will try to prevent any rise at a time like this," said Allen Huang, a manager for National Securities.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Tuesday that the stock market had "risen slightly too much", triggering fears that the government would try to curb the index.
Brokers expect the index to continue climbing on Friday. A 7,650-7,730 range was seen.
